Full custom browser own API executes. Native scoped resources/user/options/root boundary needs DisplayServer native-file-extra; basic native combined file/directory selection needs a backend supporting OpenAny. Inherited independent native child Window, accessibility/scaling and foreign profiles retain their owner gates. Native chooser callback lifecycle is covered by owner-queue injection, not physical chooser acceptance.

Basic filesystem chooser routes every presentation entry through DisplayServer on supported modes; unsupported basic flags/filter patterns/combined OpenAny fail explicitly. Resource/user/custom-option/root-boundary requests use the working embedded browser until native-file-extra exists. Physical native chooser acceptance and Windows/macOS/mobile/browser remain target gates.
Retained permanent static service implements recoverable desktop Linux trash and URI/file-manager launch. The rest of the operating-system API remains in its existing owner-specific rows.

Linux desktop MoveToTrash delegates to system GIO with recoverable metadata and link policy, verified in an isolated XDG child process. ShellOpen delegates SDL; Linux file manager uses folder URI fallback. Windows/macOS recoverable trash/item-selection backends and mobile/browser equivalent capabilities require target implementation. External application launch is not exercised during automated fixtures.
